claims.claim: The reviewer counts the cost of the multiple viewpoints: the reader does not stay in one character's head long enough to form a bond, so the intensity of the first-person Farseer books is lost.
claims.source: HearWriteNow blog review of The Liveship Traders
claims.quote: The reader doesn’t get to stay in one character’s head long enough

claims.claim: Hobb, quoted at Dragonsteel Nexus, describes writing an antagonist as putting on a coat and adopting the character's whole belief system.
claims.source: Robin Hobb, quoted by Tayan Hatch, Dragonsteel Books, 19 December 2024
claims.quote: You have to put it on like a coat
claims.page: section 'Now I Believe Everything You Believe'

claims.claim: Hobb, quoted at Dragonsteel Nexus, says an antagonist simply has something they want done that matters more to them than what the protagonist wants.
claims.source: Robin Hobb, quoted by Tayan Hatch, Dragonsteel Books, 19 December 2024
claims.quote: They simply have something they want to get done
claims.page: section 'Now I Believe Everything You Believe'

claims.claim: The reviewer lists among the trilogy's plot lines a family's debt being repaid by marrying a daughter to a Rain Wilds suitor.
claims.quote: married off to a Rain Wilds fellow as debt repayment

claims.claim: Elliott identifies the novel's opening paragraph as an excerpt from a document being composed inside the world, comparing it to Asimov's Encyclopedia Galactica.
claims.source: Geoffrey B. Elliott, Elliott RWI, 24 May 2019
claims.quote: an excerpt from a piece being composed within the milieu
claims.page: paragraph beginning 'The text of the novel opens'

claims.claim: Elliott reads the absent father's name, Chivalry, as asserting that he embodies honour, and his fathering of an unacknowledged bastard as a comment on chivalric constructions.
claims.source: Geoffrey B. Elliott, Elliott RWI, 24 May 2019
claims.quote: The name suggests that he is an embodiment of honor
claims.page: section 'A couple of other thoughts on the chapter'

claims.claim: Elliott notes the narrator dates his memories to about his sixth year and questions both their validity and their source.
claims.source: Geoffrey B. Elliott, Elliott RWI, 24 May 2019
claims.quote: he questions their validity and their source

claims.claim: Elliott names Hobb's recurring chapter-opening device as an Asimovian move of grounding chapters in reference materials drawn from inside the world.
claims.source: Geoffrey B. Elliott, Elliott RWI, 10 September 2021
claims.quote: the Asimovian move of grounding chapters in in-milieu reference materials
claims.page: commentary paragraph beginning 'I am taken by the reminiscence'

claims.claim: Elliott, a medievalist, says the chapter's opening passage is compelling because it enacts the piecing together of disparate and incomplete sources, and the fear of carrying other people's errors forward.
claims.source: Geoffrey B. Elliott, Elliott RWI, 10 September 2021
claims.quote: the piecing-together of disparate and not always complete sources
claims.page: commentary paragraph beginning 'I am taken by the reminiscence'

claims.claim: Elliott singles out the aphorism that closes that chapter-opening passage, in which a child sees the acorn of his daily life where a man looks back on the oak.
claims.source: Geoffrey B. Elliott quoting Hobb, Elliott RWI, 10 September 2021
claims.quote: A child sees the acorn of his daily life
claims.page: commentary paragraph beginning 'Too, there is the metaphor at the end'

claims.claim: Elliott states that Hobb is on record as affirming her continued use of the masculine as the default neutral, a practice he says he disagrees with.
claims.source: Geoffrey B. Elliott, Elliott RWI, 10 September 2021
claims.quote: affirming her continued use of the masculine as the default neutral
claims.page: commentary paragraph beginning 'Too, there is the metaphor at the end'

claims.claim: Elliott records the shape of the Rain Wilds volume's front matter: a cast of characters grouped by faction, then a formal and an informal message sent from Bingtown to Trehaug about the Traders' agreement with the dragon.
claims.source: Geoffrey B. Elliott, Elliott RWI, 15 July 2022
claims.quote: a formal and informal message sent from Bingtown to Trehaug

claims.claim: Elliott approves the shift in prefatory register between the Farseer and Rain Wilds books, saying the epistolary format supplies not just the encyclopedic but the personal, which helps the text come alive early.
claims.source: Geoffrey B. Elliott, Elliott RWI, 15 July 2022
claims.quote: not just the encyclopedic, but the personal

claims.claim: Elliott says he notes with approval the dramatis personae that opens the volume, because it is useful to know who is in the work.
claims.source: Geoffrey B. Elliott, Elliott RWI, 15 July 2022
claims.quote: I note with some approval the dramatis personæ

claims.claim: Elliott records that this chapter opens with a short in-milieu commentary on the use of herbs and intoxicants in Skill training before the narrative resumes.
claims.source: Geoffrey B. Elliott, Elliott RWI, 1 December 2021
claims.quote: a brief in-milieu commentary on the use of herbs

verdicts.trueWording: The reader doesn't get to stay in one character's head long enough to form a bond with them
verdicts.note: Raw page (HTTP 200, live). Quote verbatim in the paragraph 'The downside of the viewpoint shifts is that the magnificent intensity of Farseer is missing.' First-person limb supported by the section's opening line, 'Robin Hobb takes a break from the intense first person narrative of the Farseer Trilogy'. Review by Elle Neal, copyright 2006, updated 2017/2021.

verdicts.trueWording: You have to put it on like a coat and say, 'Now I believe everything you believe.'
verdicts.note: Live host returned HTTP 403 (Shopify bot wall); recovered via Wayback raw capture https://web.archive.org/web/20250808211906id_/... Quote verbatim under the section heading 'Now I Believe Everything You Believe'. Byline Tayan Hatch and date Dec 19, 2024 confirmed in the page's JSON-LD; interview framed as 'At Dragonsteel Nexus'.

verdicts.trueWording: They simply have something they want to get done, and it is more important to them than anything your protagonist wants to do
verdicts.note: Same Wayback raw capture as 331 (live 403). Quote verbatim in the same section, introduced by Hobb's 'They don't think of themselves as the villain.' Both limbs (the wanting, and its outranking the protagonist's want) are in the one sentence.

verdicts.trueWording: spoilt Malta is to be married off to a Rain Wilds fellow as debt repayment
verdicts.note: Raw page (HTTP 200). Quote verbatim inside the list that opens 'There are numerous plotlines running through the book.' Post is 'Book Review: The Liveship Traders by Robin Hobb', lexlingua, June 13 2012. Minor: the reviewer writes 'the book' in that sentence though the post reviews the whole trilogy; Malta's status as a daughter comes from an earlier paragraph, and the page says 'as debt repayment' without naming whose debt.

verdicts.trueWording: Its first paragraph is an excerpt from a piece being composed within the milieu, not unlike the Encyclopedia Galactica from Asimov's Foundation novels
verdicts.note: Raw page (HTTP 200). Quote verbatim; the Asimov comparison is in the same sentence. Paragraph begins 'The text of the novel opens with a chapter titled "The Earliest History."' as cited.

verdicts.trueWording: The name suggests that he is an embodiment of honor, and descriptions of the character reported by others generally confirm it
verdicts.note: Raw page (HTTP 200). Quote verbatim in the section 'A couple of other thoughts on the chapter'. Note the page hedges the second limb as a disjunction the claim flattens: the unacknowledged bastard 'suggests either a failure on his part or a comment by Hobb about the ultimately flawed nature of chivalric constructions' - the chivalric-comment reading is one of two Elliott offers, not his sole reading.

verdicts.trueWording: asserts that his memories begin on a day when he was some six years old, and he questions their validity and their source
verdicts.note: Raw page (HTTP 200). Quote verbatim in the third body paragraph, as cited; the same sentence carries the 'some six years old' limb.

verdicts.trueWording: I've noted before the Asimovian move of grounding chapters in in-milieu reference materials, something I appreciate
verdicts.note: Raw page (HTTP 200). Quote verbatim in the commentary paragraph beginning 'I am taken by the reminiscence with which the chapter opens.' 'I've noted before' supports the claim's 'recurring'.

verdicts.trueWording: the piecing-together of disparate and not always complete sources being something with which, as a medievalist, I am familiar
verdicts.note: Raw page (HTTP 200). Quote verbatim in the same commentary paragraph, which also carries 'the opening passage is particularly compelling' and 'the concern about possibly perpetuating the errors of others - intended or inadvertent - is one with which I struggle', covering the errors-forward limb.

verdicts.trueWording: Too, there is the metaphor at the end: 'A child sees the acorn of his daily life, but a man looks back on the oak.'
verdicts.note: Raw page (HTTP 200). Quote verbatim, opening the commentary paragraph cited. Elliott calls it a 'metaphor' rather than an aphorism, and writes 'at the end' without naming what it ends; context (the preceding paragraph is on the chapter-opening passage) supports the claim's reading.

verdicts.trueWording: Hobb is on record as affirming her continued use of the masculine as the default neutral, a practice with which I disagree
verdicts.note: Raw page (HTTP 200). Quote verbatim in the paragraph beginning 'Too, there is the metaphor at the end', exactly as cited; the disagreement limb is the same clause ('and I am far from alone in it').

verdicts.trueWording: The text moves on to present a formal and informal message sent from Bingtown to Trehaug, discussing the agreement between the Traders and Tintaglia
verdicts.note: Raw page (HTTP 200). Quote verbatim in the first paragraph. The faction-grouped cast is the preceding sentence ('grouping them as Keepers and Dragons, Bingtowners, the crew of the Tarman, and miscellaneous others'); 'the dragon' of the claim is Tintaglia.

verdicts.trueWording: the epistolary format adds a nice touch - not just the encyclopedic, but the personal, which helps the text start to come alive early on
verdicts.note: Raw page (HTTP 200). Quote verbatim in the final commentary paragraph, prefaced by 'I note with some approval, too, the shift in the prefatory tack'. Minor: Elliott names 'the Farseer and Tawny Man novels' as the earlier tack; the claim says 'Farseer and Rain Wilds books', dropping Tawny Man, though the entry is the Dragon Keeper front matter so the Rain Wilds side is contextual.

verdicts.trueWording: I note with some approval the dramatis personae that opens the current volume; it's nice to know who's in the work
verdicts.note: Raw page (HTTP 200). Quote verbatim (with the ae ligature as given) opening the final commentary paragraph. The reason limb reads 'it's nice to know who's in the work' where the claim says 'useful' - same substance, different adjective.

verdicts.trueWording: opens with a brief in-milieu commentary on the use of herbs and intoxicants in Skill training before pivoting to Fitz and the Fool
verdicts.note: Raw page (HTTP 200). Quote verbatim in the first paragraph; the chapter is named 'The Betrothal', and 'before pivoting to Fitz and the Fool altering Badgerlock's clothing' supports 'before the narrative resumes'.
